sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 03.09.2018 passed by Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Gangavathi, in MVC No.83/2016, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.
2. Insurer is not in appeal only claimant is in appeal for enhancement.

3. Shri Harish S.Maigur, learned counsel for claimant-appellant submitted that in an accident that occurred on 22.10.2011 involving insured lorry bearing registration no.KA-17/A-7224, claimant Kumari Laxmi D/O Sharanappa Yathnatti vs Ayyappa S/O Lingappa Pujari on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22379673/
2 Kumari Laxmi a student aged 11 years sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment, she did not recover fully and sustained physical disability.
Claiming compensation, she filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against driver, owner and insurer of offending vehicle.
4. On contest wherein insurer opposed claim petition on all grounds, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant's father as PW1 and Dr.Mallikarjun Kunachigi as PW2.
Exhibits P1 to P31 were marked.
In rebuttal, insurer got marked insurance policy as Exhibit R1 by consent.
5. On consideration, Tribunal held that claimant had sustained loss of earning capacity at 6% and awarded total compensation of Rs.59,769/-.

It was further submitted that Tribunal erred in not following ratio in case of Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another reported in AIR 2014 Supreme Court 736, while computing compensation in respect of injuries sustained by minor.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited & Another reported in AIR 2014 Supreme Court 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was submitted that claimant had sustained fracture of left tibia which was malunited assessed by PW2-Doctor at 26% to 28% to limb.
However, Tribunal considered whole body disability at meager extent of 6%.

It was further submitted that apart from said compensation, claimant was also entitled for reimbursement of actual amount spent towards medical treatment, amount spent towards incidental expenses by parents and parents loss of income during layoff period.
However, Tribunal had granted meager compensation of Rs.59,769/-, which called for enhancement.
6. On other hand Shri S.K.Kayakmath, learned counsel for respondent-insurer supported award and opposed enhancement.
It was submitted that on overall consideration, compensation awarded was adequate.

7. From above submission, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
8.
It is not in dispute that this is a minor's claim petition for compensation for injuries sustained in motor vehicle accident.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in Master Mallikarjun's case (supra) has stated in case of minors, award of compensation by applying regular method of assessment would not be feasible as they are non earning members.
Since, it is established that claimant had sustained permanent physical disability, structured formula for assessment as developed in Master Mallikarjun's case (supra) would apply.
Taking into account extent of limb disability assessed by PW2-Doctor, Tribunal considered whole body disability at 6%.
For said disability, claimant would be entitled for compensation under first slab i.e., Rs.1,00,000/-.
Apart from said amount, claimant would be entitled for reimbursement of money spent towards medical expenses, loss of income of parents during layoff period etc.
Claimant had produced medical bills for sum of Rs.13,569/-.
Considering same, it would be appropriate to award sum of Rs.20,000/- towards medical and other incidental expenses.

9. Tribunal has also awarded sum of Rs.16,200/- towards future loss of income, Rs.10,000/-
towards pain and suffering, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of amenities and Rs.10,000/- towards diet,
nourishment, attendant charges and conveyance.

As said award would not be inconformity with Kumari Laxmi D/O Sharanappa Yathnatti vs Ayyappa S/O Lingappa Pujari on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22379673/
3 ratio laid down in Master Mallikarjun's case (supra), same would be unsustainable.

entities.text: Kumari Laxmi D/O Sharanappa Yathnatti vs Ayyappa S/O Lingappa Pujari
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
claimant would be entitled for loss of income of parents during period of treatment.
Normally fractures take about three months to heal.
Taking into account notional income of parents, it would be appropriate to award sum of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of income during period of treatment.

10. Thus, claimant is entitled for re-assessed compensation as follows:-
Rs.1,00,000/- + Rs.20,000/- + Rs.20,000/-= Rs.1,40,000/-.
Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

11. Hence following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed.
ii.
Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.1,40,000/- along with interest at rate of 6% per annum as against Rs.59,769/- awarded by Tribunal.
iii. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv. Directions issued by Tribunal regarding release of compensation would proportionately apply to enhanced compensation also.
